facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 160 million years ago in the lower Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: dating to the Late Jurassic period, about 160 million years ago (lower Oxfordian)

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus lived at the end of the Jurassic period, about 156 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 156 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense

facts.statement: The fossil record for Metriacanthosaurus spans from 161.5 to 159 million years ago within the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 159 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name Metriacanthosaurus means "moderately-spined lizard".
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus (meaning "moderately-spined lizard")

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus was a medium-sized theropod with a femur measuring 80 cm in length.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus was a medium-sized theropod with a femur length of 80 cm

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Metriacanthosaurus at 1 tonne in 1988.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 1988 estimated its weight at 1 tonne

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the total length of Metriacanthosaurus to be 8 meters.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz gave a length of 8 meters (26.2 feet)

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus was named for its neural spines, which are moderately tall compared to other theropods.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus was named for the height of its neural spines, which are actually not overly tall for theropods

facts.statement: The neural spines of Metriacanthosaurus are about 1.5 times the height of the centrum, similar to Megalosaurus, Sinraptor, and Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: They are similar to other theropods such as Megalosaurus, Sinraptor, and Ceratosaurus in being 1.5 times the height of the centrum

facts.statement: The holotype specimen OUM J.12144 was discovered in 1871 by W. Parker at Jordan's Cliff near Weymouth, Dorset.
facts.quote: The holotype of Metriacanthosaurus parkeri, specimen OUM J.12144, was discovered in 1871 by W. Parker at Jordan's Cliff, near Weymouth, Dorset

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes an incomplete pelvis, dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ten tail vertebrae, thigh bones, and an incomplete shin bone.
facts.quote: The specimen includes an incomplete pelvis, several dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ten caudal vertebrae, femora (thigh bones), and an incomplete tibia (shin bone)

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene described the fossils as a new species of Megalosaurus in 1923.
facts.quote: In 1923, German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene wrote a paper on Jurassic and Cretaceous European carnivorous dinosaurs within Saurischia

facts.statement: In 1932, Friedrich von Huene reclassified the species as Altispinax parkeri.
facts.quote: In 1932, however, von Huene concluded it was a species of Altispinax, A. parkeri

facts.statement: Alick Walker established the new genus Metriacanthosaurus in 1964 because the fossils lacked the long vertebral spines of Altispinax.
facts.quote: In 1964, scientist Alick Walker decided these fossils were too different from Altispinax, as they lacked the long vertebral spines, and named the new genus Metriacanthosaurus

facts.statement: The generic name Metriacanthosaurus is derived from the Greek words for "moderate" and "spine".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego metrikos , "moderado" y akantha , "columna vertebral"

facts.statement: A second species, M. shangyanouensis, is now considered a specimen of Yangchuanosaurus shangyanouensis.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, llamada M. shangyanouensis es considerada hoy un ejemplar de Yangchuanosaurus shangyanouensis

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus is classified within the family Metriacanthosauridae.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus has since been reclassified in Metriacanthosauridae

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus is a member of the subfamily Metriacanthosaurinae.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus is considered a member of the subfamily Metriacanthosaurinae

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus belongs to the subfamily Metriacanthosaurinae along with Sinraptor and Siamraptor.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus es un miembro de la subfamilia Metriacanthosaurinae, junto con Sinraptor y Siamraptor

facts.statement: A 2007 review by Darren Naish and David Martill argued that Metriacanthosaurus and Yangchuanosaurus should remain as separate genera.
facts.quote: However, a 2007 review of British dinosaurs by Darren Naish and David Martill defending keeping the two genera taxonomically separate

facts.statement: Metriacanthosaurus lived alongside other large theropods of the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Metriacanthosaurus appears to have lived alongside other large theropods belonging to the family Megalosauridae

facts.statement: Despite being little known, the name Metriacanthosaurus appears in one of the DNA tubes in the movie Jurassic Park.
facts.quote: Aunque es muy poco conocido, su nombre aparece en uno de los tubos de ADN en la película de Jurassic Park

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz suggests the Jurassic Park DNA tube likely refers to Yangchuanosaurus shangyanouensis rather than Metriacanthosaurus parkeri.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Thomas R. Holtz, es probable que no se refiera al M. parkeri, sino al más conocido Yangchanosaurus shangyanouensis

rejected.statement: Metriacanthosaurus lived in Europe when it existed as an archipelago of islands surrounded by shallow seas.
rejected.quote: During this time, Europe formed an archipelago of islands surrounded by shallow seas

rejected.statement: Metriacanthosaurus likely represents a dispersal event from Asia into Europe during the early Late Jurassic.
rejected.quote: Metriacanthosaurus thus likely represents a dispersal event from Asia into Europe during the early Late Jurassic
